content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I hope someone can assist. We are able to create regular users with assigned phone numbers, and that works fine. However, we have a scenario where an external cloud application sends automated SMS to the [product_name] Mobile Communication Module. This provider's system only shows letters, such as 'ABC', as the sender instead of a phone number, which the module does not recognize as authorized. Is it possible to configure the [product_name] so it accepts incoming SMS from senders without a phone number? Note: We do not need to send SMS back to that sender. Thank you for your help!
From what I know, only numbers and a few special characters like '+' or '/' are allowed, but not letters.
Thank you! Would setting a user (or group) as '+*' help to resolve this?
I'm unsure, but I would assume that probably wouldn't work.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users want to enable an external cloud application to interact with the [product_name] Mobile Communication Module via SMS, but the module requires senders to have numeric phone numbers and does not support letter-based sender IDs. This restriction prevents integration with automated systems using alphanumeric identifiers. Users are looking for more flexible options to configure SMS sender validation and support broader integration possibilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] Mobile Communication Module to handle and process SMS messages from senders using alphanumeric IDs, such as those used by cloud systems, not just numeric phone numbers.
